FISEN Technologies
& FISEN Automation
Detailed Company and Capabilities Profile
Official Website Review · October 2026
Prepared by Manus AI
Based on publicly available company website information

FISEN Technologies & FISEN Automation Manus AI
1 Company Snapshot
FISEN Group presents itself as an integrated engineering group with two specialist business verticals.
FISEN Automation focuses on industrial automation and plant-floor control, while FISEN Technologies
focuses on enterprise software, cloud and digital products. The group positions the two businesses
as complementary: connecting operational technology (operational technology (OT)) with information
technology (information technology (IT)) to link production systems with enterprise data and software.
[1] [2]
Across the group, the publicly listed capability range extends from sensors, instrumentation, control
panels, programmable controllers and supervisory systems to cloud platforms, data pipelines, artificial
intelligence and executive dashboards. The group specifically highlights integration using OPC Unified
Architecture (OPC UA), Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) and enterprise resource planning
connections. These are company descriptions of its offer; they are not independent assessments of delivery
history or technical performance. [1]
The main public contact and conversion route for both verticals is the FISEN Group contact portal. The
two specialist sites link visitors to this shared destination for project enquiries, careers and several policy
pages. [3] [4] [6]
2 FISEN Group Structure and Positioning
2.1 Two specialist verticals
FISEN Automation — industrial and OT engineering. Its listed scope includes industrial automation,
process control, PLC, SCADA, DCS and HMI engineering, functional safety, industrial IoT and edge
connectivity, control-panel engineering and turnkey commissioning. The group describes this vertical as
responsible for production-floor systems and plant engineering. [1]
FISEN Technologies — software and IT engineering. Its listed scope includes custom enterprise
software, web and mobile applications, cloud and DevOps, microservices, SaaS platform engineering, AI-
driven workflows and cybersecurity. The group positions this vertical as the digital counterpart to its
industrial practice. [1] [6]
2.2 Group method and stated differentiators
The group describes a joint delivery model intended to connect control systems with enterprise software.
Its published stages are enterprise scoping and synergy assessment; a combined OT/IT architectural
blueprint; integrated engineering and factory acceptance testing; and on-site commissioning and site
acceptance testing. It describes its intended coverage as spanning physical instrumentation and controls
through cloud applications and dashboards. [1]
The group website also states that it targets high availability, promotes OT/IT cybersecurity hardening,
and offers delivery from its Pune engineering centre. It publishes a 40–60% cost-advantage claim and
references IEC 61508/61511 functional-safety compliance and IEC 62443 OT cybersecurity. These are
group-site representations; the pages do not give project-specific evidence, scope statements or third-party
certification records alongside each claim. Confirm scope and substantiation before using these claims in
procurement or marketing material. [1]

2.3 Publicly named client references
The group homepage displays Indoco Remedies, L’Oréal and P&G as industry-leader/client references.
The page does not explain the project scope, timing, business unit involved or permission basis for each
logo. Treat them as website-published references, not as independently verified case studies. [1]
3 FISEN Automation
3.1 Company profile
FISEN Automation describes itself as an industrial automation engineering firm serving manufacturing
and process industries. Its About page says the company has helped these sectors modernize through
turnkey automation, PLC and SCADA programming, custom control panels, machine automation and
functional-safety engineering. It frames its role around industrial automation, Industry 4.0, industrial IoT
and engineering solutions, with a stated goal of building scalable and secure connected operations. [5]
The homepage hero emphasizes mission-critical industrial control and next-generation manufacturing. It
says its turnkey systems use Siemens, Allen-Bradley and Schneider controllers, high-availability SCADA
and distributed I/O architecture. Its rotating feature topics include PLC/SCADA control, industrial IoT,
functional safety, and home/building IoT. [4]
3.2 Services and technical capabilities
3.2.1 Turnkey industrial automation and control systems
FISEN Automation lists turnkey PLC, SCADA and HMI engineering, distributed control systems (distrib-
uted control system (DCS)), safety systems and variable-frequency drive (variable-frequency drive (VFD))
integration. Its more detailed control-systems description adds custom PCC/MCC panels, process automa-
tion, validation and functional-safety verification. The site states SIL 2 and SIL 3 verification; the exact
certification status, project boundaries and assessment body are not specified on the page. [4]
3.2.2 PLC and HMI programming
The listed work includes modular PLC logic using IEC 61131-3 standards, operator-focused HMI touch-
screens, alarm logging and troubleshooting guides. The site presents these as part of its industrial control
and machine/process automation offer. [4]
3.2.3 SCADA, monitoring and reporting
SCADA capabilities described include interactive real-time plant mimic screens, automatic shift and batch
report generation, alarm paging through SMS or email, and historian archiving. The homepage also refers
to high-availability SCADA and plant monitoring. [4]
3.2.4 Control-panel design and manufacturing
The company lists electrical drawings prepared in EPLAN or AutoCAD Electrical, busbar sizing and
thermal calculations, and simulated factory acceptance testing (factory acceptance test (FAT)) before
dispatch. Its wider description includes PCC/MCC panel design and VFD drives. [4]
3.2.5 Industrial IoT and edge intelligence
FISEN Automation describes edge-gateway and telemetry-hardware integration; real-time pipelines using
OPC UA, MQTT and Modbus; predictive machine-health and vibration analysis; and cloud or on-premises

overall equipment effectiveness (overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)) dashboards. This scope connects
field equipment and plant data to operational analytics. [4]
3.2.6 Process automation, instrumentation and validation
The published process-engineering scope includes ISA-88 batch execution and recipe management, tuning
temperature, pressure, flow and level transmitters, and automating clean-in-place (clean-in-place (CIP))
and sterilize-in-place (sterilize-in-place (SIP)) operations. Its computer system validation (computer system
validation (CSV)) page lists GAMP 5 lifecycle documents (URS, FRS, SDS and TM), IQ/OQ/PQ protocol
generation and execution, and 21 CFR Part 11 audit trails and data-integrity controls. [4]
3.2.7 Functional safety and machine automation
Functional safety is named in the hero, About page and services. The site lists safety systems and SIL 2/
SIL 3 verification. The About page describes full-lifecycle coverage from feasibility and HAZOP through
hardware/control-logic design, fabrication, site testing and commissioning. The homepage’s feature
carousel also identifies machine automation, special-purpose machines, VFD/servo drives and process
control among its named areas. [4] [5]
3.3 Technology ecosystem and standards
The Automation homepage names Siemens, Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Schneider, ABB and Mitsubishi. Its
About page additionally lists Honeywell and Emerson. The pages describe a multi-vendor engineering
capability; they do not enumerate which products or versions are supported for every service. [4] [5]
Standards, protocols and regulatory terms named on the site include IEC 61131-3 for PLC logic; ISA-88 for
batch control; OPC UA, MQTT and Modbus for data exchange; GAMP 5 and 21 CFR Part 11 for regulated
computerized systems; and SIL references for safety engineering. The group homepage separately refer-
ences IEC 61508/61511 and IEC 62443. These references describe the site’s stated engineering context and
should not be read as confirmation that every project or facility holds a particular certification. [1] [4]
3.4 Delivery framework
The Automation homepage outlines five stages:
• Discovery and scoping: site visits, interviews and reviews of existing systems, constraints and objec-
tives.
• System design: preparation and review of P&IDs, functional specifications, architecture diagrams,
safety classification and platform selection.
• Engineering and development: PLC/SCADA programming, control logic, safety interlocks, HMI
design, FAT testing and version-controlled engineering.
• Commissioning and handover: site installation, site acceptance testing (site acceptance test (SAT)),
loop checks, operator training and documentation.
• Ongoing support: the site advertises 24/7 remote monitoring, SLA-backed maintenance, logic tuning,
calibration and upgrade pathways.
These are the published process descriptions; the exact scope, service levels and availability depend on a
project agreement. [4]

3.5 Industries and example solution themes
The Automation homepage gives six industry-specific examples. Its About page lists a broader set of
sectors. The examples below summarize the use cases stated on the site, not named project case studies.
[4] [5]
• Oil and gas: high-availability DCS, safety instrumented systems (safety instrumented system (SIS)),
emergency shutdown (emergency shutdown (ESD)) and pipeline monitoring for upstream, midstream
and downstream environments, with attention to hazardous-area requirements.
• Energy and power: SCADA, IEC 61850 substation automation, conventional and renewable generation
integration, and predictive maintenance.
• Automotive manufacturing: robotic cell integration, conveyor tracking, manufacturing execution
systems and real-time OEE visibility.
• Pharmaceuticals and life sciences: ISA-88 batch control, electronic batch records, track-and-trace
serialization and validation aligned with the site’s GAMP 5 and 21 CFR Part 11 references.
• Food and beverage: recipe management, packaging-line synchronization, and CIP systems for hygiene
and product-quality needs.
• Metals and mining: ruggedized control architectures, heavy-drive coordination and remote asset
monitoring for harsh environments.
The About page also names infrastructure and utilities, material handling and logistics, smart buildings/
home automation, water and wastewater, and general manufacturing/industrial processing. These appear
as served or targeted sectors, but the page provides less detail than it does for the six homepage examples.
[5]
3.6 Company details and published performance claims
The Automation About page displays 96+ projects delivered, 5+ countries served, 10+ years experi
ence and a 94% uptime SLA. The homepage’s process section separately refers to a delivery framework
built from 500+ projects, while the homepage/footer also says the company delivers across 5+ countries
and has 10+ years. The two project counts do not match. [4] [5]
Use these figures as quoted website claims only until FISEN confirms a current authoritative set, its
definition of “project,” the measurement period and the meaning of the uptime figure. The pages do not
explain the denominator or measurement method behind the 94% uptime SLA.
4 FISEN Technologies
4.1 Company profile
FISEN Technologies describes itself as the UAE-based IT-services and proprietary SaaS-products vertical
of FISEN Group, headquartered in Dubai. It says it engineers bespoke cloud software, enterprise platforms
and proprietary products for global markets. The homepage positions its work around high-performance
custom software, scalable web applications and robust backend systems for mission-critical operations. [6]
The group site summarizes the Technologies vertical as custom enterprise software, modern web apps,
cross-platform mobile apps, cloud solutions, DevOps, microservices and AI-enabled workflows. [1]
4

4.2 Services and capabilities
4.2.1 Application development
The site lists enterprise application architecture, cross-platform desktop and mobile applications, and
custom API integrations. Its description emphasizes custom software, business portals and integrations
between data and user experiences. [6]
4.2.2 Web application development
Listed capabilities include modern UI/UX design, scalable backend APIs and database optimization. The
homepage’s positioning also includes scalable web applications and backend systems. [6]
4.2.3 AI and intelligent workflows
The page names custom Claude LLM integration and workflows, computer vision, intelligent document
processing, predictive maintenance and operations analytics. The site presents these as AI-driven enter-
prise capabilities; it does not publish detailed implementation examples or customer case studies on the
homepage. [6]
4.2.4 Cloud, infrastructure and DevOps
The listed infrastructure services include architecture on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud; Kubernetes and
Docker orchestration; and automated CI/CD pipelines. The broader technology banner also names cloud
architecture, microservices, APIs and SaaS platform engineering. [6]
4.2.5 Cybersecurity and governance
The site lists a team described as certified in CISSP, CEH, CISM and CISA; security testing and VAPT; SOC
2, PCI, GDPR and HIPAA-related compliance support; and virtual CISO/DPO governance. The wording
indicates offered expertise and compliance-related services. It does not specify which entity or service
holds which certification, the audit scope, or whether any particular FISEN system is certified or compliant.
Confirm the exact personnel, certifications, assessment scope and contractual deliverables before relying
on them. [6]
4.3 Proprietary software products
The Technologies homepage says it operates four proprietary platforms across property technology, multi-
tenant cloud CRM, workforce mobility and residential community management. It describes the suite
as having 100% in-house IP and publishes a suite-level 99.99% SLA uptime figure. Those are company-
published statements; detailed ownership records and uptime calculation periods are not provided on the
page. [6]
4.3.1 Falcon CRM
Falcon CRM is described as a multi-tenant cloud sales and operations platform. Published functions include
contacts and accounts, multi-entity business management, open leads, active deals, visual pipeline stages,
sales-order workflows, quotes, invoices, approvals, credit notes, inventory, revenue intelligence, activity
scheduling and a help centre. The site describes it as a consolidated enterprise sales/deal cockpit. [6]
The product section publishes three performance figures: 99.98% SLA/uptime, a less than 45 millisec
ond query benchmark, and 500,000+ leads handled. It does not publish the measurement window,
system boundary, test setup, data source or independent verification. These figures should be treated as

product-page claims, not guaranteed service terms. The page’s product-specific 99.98% figure also differs
from the suite-level 99.99% figure. [6]
4.3.2 Smart Attendance & Workforce App
The product is described as a workforce app with geofenced biometric attendance. The accessible product
description does not provide further details about device support, biometric method, privacy controls,
integrations, reporting or deployment model. [6]
4.3.3 Being Home Society
Being Home Society is listed as a residential/community platform with the tagline “Connect · Manage
· Live Better.” The homepage gives no additional feature breakdown, user roles, integrations or service
territory in the extracted product description. [6]
4.3.4 Being Home Realty
Being Home Realty is described as a real-estate and off-plan marketplace. The FISEN Technologies
homepage links the product to beinghomerealty.ae. This report does not infer marketplace features beyond
that description. [6]
4.4 Software delivery framework
The Technologies homepage outlines four stages:
• Architecture and technical discovery: review of product requirements, existing code, performance
constraints and security/compliance objectives.
• System design and blueprinting: documentation of microservices, data schemas, API contracts, cloud
topologies and CI/CD pipelines for review and approval.
• Agile sprint engineering: two-week sprint cycles, automated unit and integration tests, Jira/Slack
updates and managed code commits.
• VAPT and quality verification: vulnerability scanning, OWASP Top 10 penetration testing, load
testing and SOC 2 readiness checks.
The site presents this as its engagement methodology. It does not state that every project follows the same
tools, timetable or scope. [6]
4.5 Technology stack named on the site
The Technologies homepage names React 19, Next.js, Node.js and Python; cloud services on AWS, Azure
and Google Cloud; Kubernetes and Docker; APIs and microservices; LLMs and computer vision; and
cybersecurity/VAPT. It also advertises SaaS platform engineering and offshore dedicated engineering pods.
The site does not give a full standard architecture, supported versions beyond named examples, or a
detailed staffing model. [6]
4.6 Case studies and recruitment
The homepage footer links to “Case Studies,” but the page content reviewed does not provide detailed
case studies with client names, project scope, timelines or measured outcomes. Careers and contact links
route to the group portal. No job openings or role-specific requirements are detailed on the Technologies
homepage itself. [6]

5 Locations, Contact and Enquiry Routes
The FISEN Group contact page lists two centres. Pune, Maharashtra, India is described as supporting
industrial automation, embedded hardware and plant engineering labs, with listed hours Monday to Friday,
9:00 AM–6:00 PM IST. Dubai & RAK, UAE is described as supporting enterprise software, SaaS products
and regional advisory; the address shown is RAKEZ Compass Centre, Al Shohada Road, Ras al-Khaimah,
UAE, with listed hours Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM GST. [3]
The public email shown by the group and both vertical sites is info@fisengroup.com. The Group contact
form asks for full name, work email, phone/WhatsApp, company, service/division and project overview.
The listed divisions include industrial automation, home automation, and Technologies/software/custom
services. [3]
The sites direct visitors to the shared FISEN Group contact form for quotes, project conversations and
contact with engineering leadership. The public pages reviewed do not show a separate Automation or
Technologies telephone number. [3] [4] [6]
6 Published Metrics: Reconciliation Needed
Several website metrics are not aligned across pages. This matters if the information is being reused in a
company website, proposal, pitch, procurement response or investor document.
• FISEN Automation project count: About page says 96+ delivered; homepage process copy says 500+
projects. No reconciliation is given. [4] [5]
• Group delivery history: Group About page says 30+ projects, 1+ countries and 3+ years of combined
legacy. The group homepage’s extracted counters display 0+ for projects, countries and years. The pages
therefore do not present a consistent set. [1] [2]
• Uptime: Automation About page says 94% uptime SLA; group homepage says its engineering is for
99.99% operational uptime; Technologies homepage says 99.99% SLA uptime for its product suite; Falcon
CRM lists 99.98%. The scope and measurement methods differ or are not disclosed. [1] [5] [6]
• Countries served: Automation pages say 5+ countries; Group About page says 1+ countries. These
may refer to different business scopes or periods, but the pages do not explain the difference. [2] [5]
• Compliance and certification language: The Technology page combines personnel certifications and
compliance-related service claims without detailing audit scope. Group safety/security standards appear
as broad corporate statements. Confirm the precise scope and evidence before using these as formal
compliance representations. [1] [6]
The metrics above are reproduced as public website claims, not independently checked performance data.
FISEN should confirm the authoritative values, dates, definitions and evidence before the figures are carried
into new collateral.
7 Acronym Glossary
The following terms are used in the company pages and this profile. Definitions are short explanations for
readers; they are not additional company claims.
API – application programming interface: A defined software interface that allows applications or
services to exchange data or request functionality.
7

FISEN Technologies & FISEN Automation Manus AI
CI/CD – continuous integration and continuous delivery/deployment: Automated practices for integrat-
ing, testing, and delivering software changes.
CIP – clean-in-place: Cleaning process for equipment interiors without dismantling the equipment.
CSV – computer system validation: Documented evidence that a computerized system is fit for its
intended regulated use.
DCS – distributed control system: A distributed architecture for controlling complex continuous or
process operations.
ESD – emergency shutdown: A protective shutdown function or system for responding to defined
emergency conditions.
FAT – factory acceptance test: A test performed before shipment or installation to confirm that equipment
meets agreed requirements.
HMI – human-machine interface: The screens and controls through which operators monitor or interact
with automation systems.
IIoT – industrial internet of things: Connected industrial sensors, equipment, gateways, and data systems.
IT – information technology: Computing systems used to store, process, secure, and exchange informa-
tion.
LLM – large language model: A machine-learning model trained to process and generate natural language.
MQTT – Message Queuing Telemetry Transport: A lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol
often used for telemetry and connected devices.
OEE – overall equipment effectiveness: A production measure commonly combining equipment avail-
ability, performance, and quality.
OPC UA – OPC Unified Architecture: An industrial communication standard for interoperable, structured
data exchange.
OT – operational technology: Hardware and software used to monitor and control physical processes and
industrial equipment.
P&ID – piping and instrumentation diagram: A process drawing showing equipment, piping, instrumen-
tation, and control relationships.
PLC – programmable logic controller: An industrial computer that executes control logic for machines
and processes.
SAT – site acceptance test: A test performed at the installation site to confirm the installed system meets
agreed requirements.
SCADA – supervisory control and data acquisition: Systems for supervisory monitoring, data collection,
alarms, and control across industrial operations.
SIP – sterilize-in-place: Sterilization process for equipment interiors without dismantling the equipment.
SIS – safety instrumented system: A system designed to bring a process to a safe state when specified
hazardous conditions arise.
VAPT – vulnerability assessment and penetration testing: Security testing that identifies weaknesses
and assesses exploitability.
VFD – variable-frequency drive: A controller that adjusts an electric motor's speed by varying the
frequency and voltage supplied to it.
